seoTitle: Free Glob Pattern Tester for File Paths
metaDescription: Test glob patterns such as src/**/*.{js,ts} against a list of file paths. See which pattern matches each path. Free and local.
intro: Paste glob patterns and a list of paths to see which paths match. Supports *, **, ?, character classes, brace lists, extglob and exclusions.
why:
Globs are used in build tools, linters, CI configs and shells, and small differences cause missed or extra files. Testing a pattern against real paths before you commit it saves a failed build.

The tool turns each glob into a regular expression and tests every path. Patterns starting with ! exclude, and the last matching pattern decides. Names starting with a dot are skipped by * and ** unless you allow them, as in bash. Real tools differ in details, so use this as a close check, not a final word.
howTo: Enter glob patterns, one per line. Start a line with ! to exclude.
Paste your file paths, one per line.
Set the options for dotfiles, base name matching and case.
Read which pattern matched each path.

faq.a: It follows common bash and minimatch behaviour: * and ? stay within one folder, ** crosses folders, braces expand, and [abc] and [!abc] are classes. Differences between tools exist.

faq.q: Why is a dotfile not matched by *?
faq.a: Shells and most glob libraries hide names that start with a dot unless the pattern names the dot or an option allows it. Tick the dot option to include them.
